subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: Which committed-state invariant should synchronous authorization reads use while the same process owns an asynchronous exec-approval write lock?
rationale: The current bypass is unsafe with the in-place copy fallback, while choosing between a committed snapshot and unified process-local coordination affects a security-sensitive persistence boundary.

options.title: Serve committed snapshot
options.body: Keep the last validated committed policy available to synchronous readers until the active writer successfully publishes its replacement.

options.title: Unify lock coordination
options.body: Replace the split synchronous and asynchronous ownership paths with one process-local coordinator that preserves read/write serialization.

options.title: Accept lockless reads
options.body: Permit readers during writes and explicitly accept temporary partial or fail-closed policy observations from fallback copies.

recommendation.title: Serve committed snapshot
recommendation.body: Keep the last validated committed policy available to synchronous readers until the active writer successfully publishes its replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to both exec-approval security behavior and the shared filesystem-safety architecture.
